answer: Attention-sink delay channels: each new identity must complete a sequence of unpredictable micro-tasks whose completion times feed an inlet of randomized hold periods; release is gated on accumulated dwell that cannot be parallelized or delegated cheaply. A zephyr of short idle gaps is inserted so scripts gain nothing from batching. Attacker cost: sustained human-equivalent attention hours per identity plus idle waiting, making mass registration economically negative. Basalt-stable audit logs prevent replay of completed channels.
